pr_title: Improve DateTime error handling and add some bad date tests
pr_body:
Catch any `DateTimeException` as some may not be caught during parsing phase and only come up during `from` phase. 

Also add some bad date tests. 

Fixes https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/issues/112190

comments: @craigtaverner Could you provide an example of the query/date that leads to this failure?

> [@craigtaverner](https://github.com/craigtaverner) Could you provide an example of the query/date that leads to this failure?

I was not able to see the query in the server logs. This was not a CI test failure, but an issue in a cloud instance. I speculate the user entered an invalid date with an invalid month, eg. "2024-0-1"

review_comments: I see tests for `0` month and `0` days. I'm curious what happens with `0` years?
I think 0 years should be valid? I mean there's no actual year 0 in UTC/Gregorian, but Java treats year 0 as 1 BCE and it's a valid date I think.

In the [main parse method](https://github.com/elastic/elasticsearch/blob/main/server/src/main/java/org/elasticsearch/common/time/JavaDateFormatter.java#L185) we just catch `Exception`, and throw `IllegalArgumentException` - could we just do the same here?
I'm not sure, catching `Exception` kinda makes me feel uneasy usually, is it ok in this context? Usually I prefer to specify.
